brief: Make this screen recording snappy: cut pauses, speed the slow part, zoom on clicks, captions.
requirements: the input is the named screen recording (one source — 'this screen recording'; it is missing: flagged in feasibility, never invented or redrawn)
cut pauses: the idle and silent stretches are removed (measured from the ingest silence map — dead time cut, not guessed)
speed the slow part: the identified slow passage is sped up (a time remap above 1x on that passage only — the rest plays at 1x)
the slow part is identified from the recording itself (a stated method — silence map or hold detection, not an arbitrary timecode)
zoom on clicks: punch-in zooms at the click moments (the zooms land on the actual clicks, found from the recording — cursor or click detection, not random beats)
captions: burned-in captions plus SRT/VTT (explicitly asked; the caption text carries the actions or steps shown)
snappy overall: the result is tight (subjective — critic evidence; measured: much shorter than the source, no long static holds)
captions and zoomed content stay inside the safe area (the punch-ins keep the action and the caption band on-screen)
no duration or format was named: the plan states its assumptions (the target length after the cuts; the recording's own aspect — 16:9)
must_not: inventing the screen recording (it is missing: flagged in feasibility — never fabricated, never redrawn as a mock UI)
cutting pauses by guesswork (the silence map from ingest measures them: dead time is measured, not vibes)
the speed-up applied to the whole recording (only the slow part is sped: the rest plays at 1x)
zooms at arbitrary times (the punch-ins land on the actual clicks — found from the recording, not on random beats)
dropping the captions (they are explicitly asked)
